subject: quantitative_aptitude
question: In a research institute of 120 scientists, each scientist studies at least one of the three languages: Python, R, and Julia. 65 study Python, 55 study R, and 45 study Julia. Exactly 20 scientists study both Python and R, 15 study both R and Julia, and 18 study both Python and Julia. What is the number of scientists who study EXACTLY TWO of these three languages?
explanation: Given n(P ∪ R ∪ J) = 120. By 3-set union formula: 120 = 65 + 55 + 45 - (20 + 15 + 18) + n(all 3) => 120 = 165 - 53 + n(all 3) => n(all 3) = 120 - 112 = 8. The count of scientists studying exactly two languages is given by: Sum of two-set intersections - 3 × n(all three) = (20 + 15 + 18) - 3(8) = 53 - 24 = 29.
